card.name: Sanjuanito
card.era: Pre-Hispanic roots asserted; popularized from early 20th c. (origins contested)
card.tagline: Festive Andean 2/4 dance-genre, an Ecuadorian national music.
card.profile: Sanjuanito is an Indigenous and mestizo festive dance and music genre of the Ecuadorian Sierra, originating in Imbabura Province and associated with (though not exclusive to) the Otavalo people (English Wikipedia). Written in 2/4 with pentatonic melodies in minor mode, it is tied to the Fiestas de San Juan (24 June), coinciding with Inti Raymi. Indigenous versions feature dancers circling central musicians playing two flutes and a bombo; mestizo and Pan-Andean versions add guitar, rondador, bandolin, violin, accordion and quena (EcuadorUniversitario; La Hora).
card.insight: Considered an Ecuadorian national rhythm, it should not be confused with the Colombian 'sanjuanero,' a distinct bambuco song from Huila (Q7418595). Ecuador's FUNPAE has petitioned the Ministry of Culture and INPC for national heritage status (English Wikipedia; La Hora).
